intro.title: Props Drilling
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple React application with TypeScript to understand props drilling. You will create a component hierarchy where data is passed down from a parent component to deeply nested child components through props. The core concept you'll learn is how to manage and pass data between components without using state management libraries, which is a fundamental React pattern. You'll work with functional components, TypeScript interfaces for type-safe props, and the JSX syntax for rendering. By the end, you'll see how props drilling works in practice and recognize its use cases and limitations.
intro.usecase: Props drilling is a common pattern in React applications where data needs to flow through multiple intermediate components to reach deeply nested child components. You'll encounter this when building complex UI structures like e-commerce product pages where user selections (size, color) must pass from the main product component down to cart buttons, or in dashboard applications where user preferences cascade from settings panels to individual chart widgets. This pattern appears in form-heavy applications where validation state or input values need to reach nested field components, and in content management systems where editing controls pass through layout wrappers to reach specific content blocks. Understanding props drilling helps you manage data flow in real-world component hierarchies before exploring more advanced state management solutions.
